author: Pontoppidan, 1763
summary: 봄과 가을에 작은 무리를 지어 한반도 동해안과 서해안을 지나가는 나그네새이다. 지렁이, 갑각류, 조개, 곤충을 즐겨 먹는다. 시베리아의 북극 툰드라에서 번식하며, 이끼로 덮인 마른 구릉의 오목한 곳에 둥지를 틀고 한배에 알 4개를 낳는다. 동남아시아, 오스트레일리아, 아프리카에서 겨울을 난다.

points.ko: 밤색 얼굴과 멱, 흰 턱 밑
points.en: chestnut face and throat with white chin
black mantle and scapulars fringed chestnut
chestnut neck, breast and belly with white fringes

sexes.male: 여름깃 수컷은 얼굴과 아랫면 전체가 짙은 적갈색(벽돌색)이다.
sexes.female: 여름깃 암컷은 적갈색이 옅고 칙칙하며, 아랫면 특히 배에 흰 깃 끝이 많이 섞인다.

young: 어린새는 윗면 깃이 흑갈색~회갈색에 흰색·황갈색 테가 있어 비늘무늬처럼 보이고, 목과 가슴은 엷은 황갈색을 띠며 세로줄이 거의 없다.

similar.how: 민물도요보다 다리와 목이 길고 부리가 더 길게 아래로 휘었으며, 날 때 흰 허리가 뚜렷하다.

art.subject: Curlew Sandpiper (Calidris ferruginea), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean coastal mudflats in late April and May: face, neck and entire underparts deep brick-red to chestnut, with narrow whitish fringes on the belly in fresh plumage; crown rufous streaked black; a small whitish area around the bill base and a white chin; mantle and scapulars black with chestnut and pale grey-white fringes; undertail coverts white. Bill black, long and smoothly decurved; dark eye; black legs.
art.pose: feeding in a small flock on wet mud, side view
art.scene: Korean coastal mudflat during spring migration, wet mud along the shore; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding (late April–May), side view standing: brick-red to chestnut face, neck and underparts with fine white fringes, rufous black-streaked crown, black scapulars fringed chestnut, white chin, long evenly decurved black bill, black legs
adult male breeding, head detail in side view: chestnut face and throat, small white chin and whitish feathering at the bill base, long black bill curving down evenly from base to tip
in flight, seen from above: dark upperparts, narrow white wing-bar, square white rump patch above a grey tail
art.build: Slim, elegant sandpiper, about 22cm, a little larger than a Dunlin with a longer neck, longer legs and a more upright stance. Bill black, clearly longer than the head and evenly curved downward along its whole length, finest at the tip. Legs black and fairly long, the tibia well exposed. Long wings: the folded wingtips reach slightly beyond the tail tip. In flight a clear white wing-bar and a square, unmarked white rump contrasting with the darker back and grey tail.
avoid: Do not paint a bill that droops only near the tip; that is Dunlin (Calidris alpina). The Curlew Sandpiper's bill curves evenly along its whole length.
Do not paint a black belly patch (breeding Dunlin).
Do not paint a dark-centred rump in flight; the rump is pure white.
Do not paint a short straight bill on a stocky body; that is Red Knot (Calidris canutus), which also has red underparts.
Do not paint yellow or greenish legs.
